expectations.text: States it is not legal advice and routes the clause itself to counsel.
expectations.evidence: "Not legal or insurance advice... Counsel owns the contract wording, including the cancellation and force-majeure clauses."

expectations.text: Places an internal go/no-go decision date just before each fee step-up in the schedule, never after one.
expectations.evidence: 23 Nov is 10 days before the 3 Dec cliff; 5 Jan is 12 days before the 17 Jan cliff.

expectations.text: Converts the days-out thresholds (180, 90 and 45 days) into calendar dates counted back from 3 March.
expectations.evidence: Table: "Up to 4 Sep 2026", "5 Sep – 3 Dec 2026", "4 Dec 2026 – 17 Jan 2027", "From 18 Jan 2027".

expectations.text: Rejects or corrects the proposed monthly cadence, on the grounds that a round-number interval can land after a step-up.
expectations.evidence: "14 Dec lands after the first cliff. The team will have paid $49k to wait."

expectations.text: Ties a decision date to each of the schedule's boundaries (25%, 50%, 75%, 100%) rather than only to the final cliff.
expectations.evidence: The 25% step has lapsed and is flagged. Checkpoints sit before the 3 Dec (50→75%) and 17 Jan (75→100%) cliffs.

expectations.text: States that the fee curve steps rather than rising smoothly, and that each step is a date on which waiting became materially more expensive.
expectations.evidence: "Waiting costs $0 inside a band and $49k at each of two cliffs."

expectations.text: Says the threshold for each polled area must be written and agreed before the first decision date arrives, not decided inside the meeting.
expectations.evidence: "Thresholds to fix before 23 Nov. Agree these with the VP now, while nobody is under pressure."

expectations.text: Explains that fixing thresholds in advance is the defence against a team talking itself past its own limit once sunk cost is high.
expectations.evidence: "$196k of committed minimum is more than a team under sunk-cost pressure should adjudicate live."

expectations.text: Treats the 85% pickup requirement on 240 room nights as a second, parallel financial cliff on its own schedule, separate from the cancellation-fee curve.

expectations.text: Recommends negotiating cumulative attrition rather than day-by-day, or renegotiating the block size before the penalty triggers rather than arguing it afterwards.

expectations.text: Recommends the polled go/no-go format in which each area owner votes go or no-go and a single no-go halts the sequence.

expectations.text: Names the areas to poll, including registration or ticket pace against break-even, room-block pickup against the attrition threshold, and contractual exposure (which deadlines have already passed).
